paragraphs: Mamba processes sequences efficiently by allowing its internal parameters to depend on the input. That flexibility complicates stability analysis: even when individual update matrices are stable, switching between them can produce an unbounded internal trajectory. The paper uses control theory to analyze the resulting system rather than inferring stability from successful empirical performance.

The authors interpret selective scans as samples of a continuous-time linear system and prove bounded-input, bounded-output stability. In plain language, bounded inputs lead to bounded outputs under the analyzed formulation. They also derive robustness bounds containing two terms that grow linearly with sequence length, quantifying how sensitivity can accumulate as sequences become longer.

For more general systems whose parameters vary, the paper supplies conditions based on a common quadratic Lyapunov function, a shared mathematical certificate of stability. Algorithms extract the relevant certificate constants directly from network weights. The resulting guarantees concern individual selective state-space layers, making them a concrete step toward verifiable deployment guarantees rather than a certification of an entire deployed model.
icml-2026-a-control-theoretic-view-of-ma.tldr: A control-theoretic analysis provides stability proofs, robustness bounds, and weight-based certificates for individual selective state-space layers.

paragraphs: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model by training only a limited set of parameters. This paper questions the usual choice to keep that allocation fixed throughout training. Its premise is that the regions most useful to optimize can change as adaptation progresses, so an initially sensible allocation may stop matching the model’s current needs.

Dynamic Adaptive Fine-tuning, or DAF, periodically reassesses the model using a context-aware sensitivity analysis and then changes which structures remain trainable. Its Rebuild-and-Refocus strategy freezes modules that are no longer the current priority, preserving what they have learned. It redirects the available parameter budget toward regions newly identified as important.

Experiments on challenging vision benchmarks report significant improvements over mainstream methods with static allocations, including better performance and efficiency under especially restrictive parameter budgets. These findings support treating parameter allocation as part of the optimization process itself. The contribution is a mechanism for repeatedly deciding where adaptation effort is most valuable while retaining knowledge from earlier training stages.
icml-2026-beyond-static-allocation-dynam.tldr: DAF periodically reallocates trainable parameters toward newly important model regions, improving vision adaptation under tight parameter budgets.

paragraphs: A process-monitoring system needs features that remain useful when operating conditions change. Features that predict faults in one environment may also reflect shifts in ordinary operating behavior. This paper addresses that tension by combining temporal relevance with resistance to changes in feature means across environments, rather than optimizing either property alone.

Causal Feature Learning formulates feature extraction as a generalized Rayleigh-quotient problem. Its objective rewards correlation with target variables while penalizing sensitivity to environment-dependent mean shifts. This creates a mathematical trade-off between predictive information and a specific form of environmental stability. The theoretical analysis establishes conditions under which the method recovers a predictive subspace whose means are invariant across environments.

On the Tennessee Eastman Process, the method achieves an average fault detection rate of 94.6%, outperforming 15 baselines while recording the lowest realized false-alarm rate and detection delay. These results indicate that the chosen balance can help distinguish faults from changing operating conditions. The theoretical guarantee is conditional and specifically concerns mean invariance, preserving the scope of what the analysis establishes.
icml-2026-causal-feature-learning-via-ge.tldr: Causal Feature Learning balances temporal prediction with environment mean invariance to improve fault detection under changing operating conditions.

paragraphs: Many statistical problems specify how plausible each outcome is without supplying the normalization needed to turn those scores into probabilities. Diffusion samplers learn a reusable process for drawing samples from such distributions. This paper develops that approach for discrete spaces, where outcomes take distinct values and techniques developed for continuous sampling have been less fully explored.

The main contribution introduces off-policy training techniques for discrete diffusion samplers, bringing a training idea used in continuous-space sampling into the discrete setting. Experiments on established and newly introduced synthetic benchmarks show improved sampler performance. The focus is on improving how the sampling process is learned, so the learned process can subsequently generate samples efficiently.

The authors also extend the framework to connect two arbitrary distributions through discrete diffusion bridges. They introduce discrete data-to-energy Schrödinger bridge training and demonstrate data-free posterior sampling inside the discrete latent spaces of image generators. Together, these contributions expand discrete diffusion from sampling a single energy-defined target toward learning connections between distributions and supporting inference within generative models.
icml-2026-discrete-diffusion-samplers-an.tldr: Off-policy training improves discrete diffusion samplers, while new bridge formulations extend them to distribution matching and latent-space posterior sampling.

paragraphs: Multiple kernel learning combines several ways of measuring similarity between examples. As with an ensemble, a collection can benefit from members that contribute different information. This paper targets two weaknesses in existing approaches: insufficient attention to diversity among kernels and the tendency of traditional kernels to treat all input features as equally important.

DARFMMKL combines Recursive Feature Machine kernels, which learn feature importance from data, with a selection procedure that considers both kernel quality and diversity. Selecting the collection leads to a difficult binary optimization problem. The authors use Glover linearization and continuous relaxation to obtain a linear program, then apply Nyström sketching to accelerate the procedure and decouple the selector’s cost from sample size.

A generalization bound explicitly connects kernel diversity with estimation error, giving diversity a role in the theoretical account as well as the selection objective. Across 12 benchmark datasets, the method consistently outperforms nine state-of-the-art multiple kernel learning methods. The results support jointly improving the individual similarity measures and the complementarity of the collection selected for learning.
icml-2026-diversity-aware-recursive-feat.tldr: DARFMMKL learns feature-sensitive kernels and selects them for both quality and diversity, improving results across 12 benchmark datasets.

paragraphs: Ropes, cables, and rubber bands challenge robots because their shapes and responses change during manipulation. Methods built around a narrow task or material have difficulty covering that variety, while collecting sufficiently diverse physical demonstrations can be impractical. DLO-Lab provides a simulation and benchmarking platform designed around these deformable linear objects.

Its differentiable simulator represents a broad range of material behaviors, including stretching constraints, elasticity, lasting changes from bending, and interactions with other objects. A task suite then tests manipulation skills against the distinctive difficulties these objects create. In particular, task success can depend strongly on the object’s topological configuration and on where the robot chooses to grasp it.

The paper also introduces an agent that proposes strategic grasp points and breaks long tasks into parts to improve control over the object. Evaluations cover multiple policy-learning algorithms and transfer from simulation to physical execution. These experiments demonstrate the platform’s potential as a shared basis for learning and comparing manipulation strategies across materials and tasks, with grasp choice and task decomposition treated explicitly.
icml-2026-dlo-lab-benchmarking-deformabl.tldr: DLO-Lab combines versatile deformable-object simulation, benchmark tasks, and a grasp-aware agent to study robotic rope and cable manipulation.

paragraphs: Dynamic scheduling benchmarks face a measurement problem: fixed instances can encourage overfitting, while uncontrolled random generation can obscure differences between algorithms. DynaSchedBench addresses this for dynamic flexible job-shop scheduling by generating instances with calibrated difficulty. Its Sequential Event-Space Calibrator uses a Schedule Stress Index to organize instances by how demanding they are.

The calibrator reaches target metrics reliably and is substantially more computationally efficient than the evolutionary baselines evaluated. The broader framework connects generation, snapshot-based simulation, agents, evaluation, and visualization. This supports comparisons of policies that react to the current situation and policies that look ahead, within a more controlled testing environment.

Using this framework, the authors find an observability paradox in step-wise online decisions: giving LLM agents complete structural information can yield worse performance than concise information. Tools and refinement add substantial token overhead without reliably helping, and most tested LLM agents do not consistently beat strong dispatching baselines. These findings characterize the evaluated agents as robust approximators of heuristics more than superior optimizers, while showing why information presentation matters.
icml-2026-dynaschedbench-calibrated-dyna.tldr: DynaSchedBench calibrates dynamic scheduling difficulty and finds that more complete information can worsen LLM agents’ scheduling decisions.

paragraphs: In multi-instance partial-label learning, each training example is a bag of instances paired with several candidate labels, only one of which is correct. The learner must identify both the relevant instances and the true label. Incorrect candidates can mislead attention mechanisms, causing them to emphasize unhelpful instances and overlook the evidence that actually distinguishes the class.

AGOPMIPL uses an average gradient outer product computed from bag-level features and the model’s prediction. This quantity provides information about feature directions associated with changes in the prediction. Incorporating it into attention amplifies discriminative directions, helping the network identify key instances. Feature prototypes and a progressive label-disambiguation strategy further suppress misleading candidate labels.

The method consistently outperforms five state-of-the-art baselines across four MIPL benchmarks and the real-world CRC-MIPL dataset. Its largest reported relative gain is 25.9% on CRC-MIPL-KMeansSeg. The results support using gradient-derived feature information alongside attention and label refinement to address the intertwined uncertainty about which instances matter and which candidate label is correct.
icml-2026-enhanced-multi-instance-partia.tldr: AGOPMIPL uses gradient-informed attention and progressive label refinement to identify useful instances despite ambiguous candidate labels.

paragraphs: Robot actions combine broad movement with small adjustments needed for accurate execution. This paper analyzes action sequences using the discrete cosine transform, which separates their slower and faster variations. The authors observe a meaningful pattern: low-frequency components describe overall trajectories, while high-frequency components capture precise timing, alignment, and contact behavior.

Causal Spectral Policy turns that observation into a hierarchy for generating actions. It first predicts coarse motion from observations and language, then generates fine corrections conditioned on the realized trajectory. This ordering gives the refinement stage a concrete motion to work with. The architecture therefore represents the dependency between task-level intent and the adjustments required to execute that intent precisely.

Across simulation and real-world evaluations, the policy consistently outperforms strong baselines on manipulation tasks that require precision. The authors also introduce a demonstration-augmentation method that injects noise inspired by human teleoperation, under which the approach shows strong robustness. Together, the results support organizing action prediction around broad trajectories and their dependent corrections, including when demonstrations contain noise.
icml-2026-hierarchical-policy-learning-v.tldr: Causal Spectral Policy predicts broad robot motions before trajectory-dependent fine corrections, improving precision-sensitive manipulation.

paragraphs: A laboratory layout must support an experimental procedure, account for chemical safety, and permit navigation. Visual plausibility alone does not establish those properties. LabBuilder tackles this by generating and verifying three-dimensional laboratory environments from short textual specifications, grounding the scene in the protocol the laboratory is intended to support.

The system connects three components. LabForge assembles annotated assets and chemical knowledge, then translates natural language requirements into structured protocols. LabGen uses those protocols in an iterative optimization process that considers layout constraints. LabTouchstone evaluates the resulting environments through a unified benchmark. This sequence links the meaning of a requested experiment to spatial design and subsequent assessment.

Experiments report significant improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods, producing realistic environments that satisfy modeled geometric, chemical-safety, and navigation constraints. The qualification about modeled constraints defines the scope of validity: the system checks the requirements represented in its framework. Its contribution is to make experimental protocols and layout-level constraints central to laboratory scene generation, connecting appearance with the conditions needed for interaction and execution.
icml-2026-labbuilder-protocol-grounded-3.tldr: LabBuilder generates laboratory layouts from textual specifications and verifies them against modeled protocol, geometry, chemical-safety, and navigation requirements.

paragraphs: Referring expression segmentation identifies the pixels belonging to an object described in language. With limited annotated examples, models can learn from unlabeled image–text pairs by creating pseudo-labels, but unreliable labels weaken that supervision. Learning to Label treats constructing and choosing these labels as a trainable decision process.

A multimodal language model first supplies semantic and spatial prior information. The framework converts this into initial soft segmentation proposals, then combines the proposals with textual cues to produce learnable guidance for a hierarchical segmentation network. Reinforced pseudo-label selection explores which pixel-level supervision is useful, assigning rewards based on the multimodal priors and the segmentation model’s predictions.

This creates a feedback loop in which the segmentation model and its pseudo-labels improve together under sparse supervision. Experiments on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg report improvements over existing methods and support the framework’s effectiveness and generalization. The central idea is that unlabeled data becomes more useful when the system learns how to supervise itself, with label selection evolving alongside the model that consumes those labels.
icml-2026-learning-to-label-a-reinforced.tldr: Learning to Label jointly improves segmentation and pseudo-label selection through multimodal guidance and reinforcement-based supervision decisions.

paragraphs: Adapting a large video generator to improve low-quality video can demand extensive training. LiteVSR keeps the entire pretrained Diffusion Transformer frozen and learns a lightweight adapter instead. Its motivation comes from a flow-matching formulation in which predicting a constant velocity across timesteps reduces adaptation to learning a fixed injection pattern.

The State-Aware Adapter still responds to the evolving restoration process. One stream extracts structural information from the low-quality input, while another extracts information from intermediate denoising states. Time-dependent cross-attention aligns the two streams, allowing the process to shift from matching structure toward refining texture as denoising advances. This combines persistent input guidance with awareness of the current generated state.

The paper reports competitive restoration quality with 11.25% trainable parameters and 12 GPU-hours of training on a single A100. The method also remains compatible with fast sampling down to one step. These findings show that the reported adaptation can be achieved through a comparatively small trainable component while retaining the frozen generator and its fast-sampling compatibility.
icml-2026-litevsr-lightweight-adaptation.tldr: LiteVSR adapts a frozen video Diffusion Transformer for super-resolution using a small adapter that combines input structure with evolving denoising states.

paragraphs: Model routing selects which language model should answer a query, balancing expected quality against inference cost. Routers built around a fixed list of models can be difficult to adapt when new models arrive or budgets change. SCOPE instead predicts the cost and performance of candidate models before making the routing decision.

Trained with reinforcement learning, SCOPE reasons from retrieved examples of how models behave on similar problems. This grounds its estimates in observed behavior rather than fixed model names and enables routing to previously unseen models. Explicit estimates of expense and accuracy also let the routing decision respond to a user’s current priorities, rather than embedding one fixed trade-off in the selector.

Experiments report accuracy improvements of up to 25.7% when performance is prioritized, or cost reductions of up to 95.1% when efficiency is prioritized. These figures describe different operating priorities, rather than a single simultaneous outcome. The findings support routing as a controllable decision process in which estimated model behavior can guide both economical and accuracy-focused choices.
icml-2026-models-under-scope-scalable-an.tldr: SCOPE predicts model cost and accuracy from behavior on similar problems, enabling flexible routing that extends to unseen models.

paragraphs: Imbalanced domain generalization concerns models that face both changing domains and unequal class frequencies. These shifts interact: a class may be common in one domain and rare in another, influencing where the model places its decision boundaries. The paper first derives a generalization bound that highlights differences in predicted class probabilities across domains and the separation provided by decision margins.

That analysis motivates Negative-Dominant Contrastive Learning, which emphasizes examples from different classes as the main contrastive signal. The method strengthens separation between classes and amplifies gradient signals for minority classes, countering decision boundaries biased toward majority classes. A reweighted cross-entropy component encourages examples from the same class to form compact groups.

A further alignment strategy operates around predictions to encourage consistent class probabilities across domains. Together, the components address class separation, within-class compactness, and cross-domain consistency. Benchmark experiments validate the method’s effectiveness. The contribution connects the theoretical quantities in the bound with training mechanisms that directly influence decision boundaries under the combined pressures of domain shift and class imbalance.
icml-2026-negatives-dominant-contrastive.tldr: NDCL emphasizes negative contrastive examples and prediction alignment to improve generalization across domains with uneven class frequencies.

paragraphs: The meaning of a table cell can depend on several nested headers, merged cells, and relationships in both row and column directions. Flattening such a table into text or forcing it into a normalized grid can obscure those relationships. Orthogonal Hierarchical Decomposition builds an input representation intended to preserve them for language-model reasoning.

Its Orthogonal Tree Induction method uses spatial and semantic constraints to produce two trees: one for column hierarchies and one for row hierarchies. A dual-pathway association protocol then reconstructs each cell’s semantic lineage through both directions. An LLM acts as a semantic arbitrator to align information across levels, helping connect a cell’s content to the nested categories that give it meaning.

The framework is evaluated on the AITQA and HiTab complex-table question-answering benchmarks, where it consistently outperforms existing representation approaches across multiple metrics. These results support explicitly representing a table’s hierarchy before asking a model to reason over it. The central contribution is a structured account of how a cell inherits meaning from both dimensions of an irregular table.
icml-2026-orthogonal-hierarchical-decomp.tldr: OHD represents complex tables through complementary row and column trees to preserve the hierarchical meaning needed for question answering.

paragraphs: Privacy-preserving language-model inference must balance concealing the input, retaining useful model behavior, and keeping computation manageable. OSNIP approaches this through a lightweight transformation performed on the client. The framework perturbs input embeddings so that their transformed representations preserve semantic fidelity while becoming nearly orthogonal to the originals.

The authors formalize the high-dimensional region supporting this combination as an Obfuscated Semantic Null Space. Their construction extends a geometric intuition from linear kernels to language-model latent spaces. A key-dependent stochastic mapping generates different perturbations when fresh keys are used. The privacy mechanism is built into the transformed representation and does not require post-processing.

Evaluations on generative and classification benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance, sharply reduced attack success rates, and strong model utility under the tested strict security constraints. These findings indicate that the proposed geometric transformation can preserve task-relevant meaning while making attacks less successful in those evaluations. The approach matters because it places the privacy transformation at the client side while addressing utility and efficiency within the same framework.
icml-2026-osnip-balancing-the-privacy-ut.tldr: OSNIP uses keyed client-side embedding perturbations to preserve semantic utility while sharply reducing attack success in reported evaluations.

paragraphs: A language model can produce a plausible reasoning chain that contains logical errors along the way. Checking only the completed response leaves those intermediate mistakes outside the feedback process. This paper introduces a framework that interleaves formal symbolic verification with natural-language generation, providing feedback as reasoning unfolds.

The framework detects and rectifies errors during generation and actively penalizes intermediate fallacies. It is implemented through two training stages: supervised fine-tuning guided by formal verification, followed by policy optimization using that guidance. Formal checks therefore influence both the examples from which the model learns and the optimization of its subsequent reasoning behavior.

Across six benchmarks covering mathematical, logical, and general reasoning, the authors report that their 7B and 14B models outperform state-of-the-art baselines by average margins of 10.4% and 14.2%, respectively. These results support formal verification as a scalable source of training feedback for stronger reasoning. The contribution is the integration of verification into the ongoing reasoning process, giving training a way to respond to the validity of intermediate steps.
icml-2026-pushing-the-boundaries-of-natu.tldr: Interleaving formal verification with language-model reasoning supplies intermediate error feedback and improves performance across six reasoning benchmarks.

paragraphs: People can often compare two outcomes more naturally than assign each a numerical reward. Pairwise preferences can also express some goals that scalar rewards cannot capture. However, existing preference-based reinforcement-learning methods struggle with long decision horizons and lack guarantees about whether policies using only the current state can match policies using the entire history.

The paper introduces a problem setting called the Markov decision contest. Within this setting, it proves that stationary Markov policies perform as well as history-dependent policies. Such policies base decisions on the current state with a rule that does not change over time. The authors also show that recovering an optimal policy exactly is a polynomial-time problem.

A simple iterative algorithm is proved to converge to an optimal policy at a sublinear rate. A deep-learning version demonstrates efficiency on long-term decision problems requiring function approximation. These contributions connect a theoretically tractable preference-based formulation with a practical learning approach. The policy-equivalence and computational guarantees apply to the introduced setting, which is the basis for resolving the concerns studied.
icml-2026-reinforcement-learning-with-pa.tldr: Markov decision contests enable long-horizon learning from pairwise preferences with optimal stationary-policy guarantees and a convergent iterative algorithm.

paragraphs: SEDRAS evaluates whether language models can infer an underlying rule from unfamiliar observations. It creates synthetic scenarios with separately controlled complexity in the data-generating logic, the representation of observations, and the way a model accesses or explores them. This modular design separates different demands involved in scientific discovery.

The model first develops an interpretable natural-language theory explaining the observations. In a separate conversation, it converts that theory into executable code, which is compared programmatically with the known data-generating distribution. This makes the proposed explanation testable against the mechanism that produced the data. The initial evaluation suite contains 600 scenarios.

Gemini 3.0 Pro achieves the best overall score, while strengths differ by task: GPT 5.2 leads on purely symbolic data, Claude Opus 4.5 on files, Gemini on non-dynamic scenarios, and Grok 4.1 as underlying-distribution complexity scales. All evaluated models struggle with active exploration and appear unable to select informative observations effectively, exploring less efficiently than a random baseline. The findings distinguish successful rule inference from the ability to decide what evidence to seek.
icml-2026-sedras-symbolically-evaluated-.tldr: SEDRAS tests model-generated scientific theories against synthetic ground truth and finds pronounced weaknesses in choosing informative observations.

paragraphs: Generating a convincing image does not necessarily place every object exactly where a requested layout specifies. The paper identifies a structural issue in masked autoregressive models: converting two-dimensional latent representations into a one-dimensional sequence weakens spatial relationships. StructMAR introduces explicit spatial structure to improve alignment between generated object instances and their intended layouts.

The framework combines two-dimensional rotary positional embeddings with an attention bias guided by the layout. These components steer latent tokens toward their corresponding object instances during attention computation. A final refinement stage uses Group Relative Policy Optimization to reduce the mismatch between the model’s training objective and the detector-based metrics used to assess layout alignment.

StructMAR reports state-of-the-art results on COCO-Position and COCO-MIG, including 57.2 AP and 79.4 mIoU on the former, and 61.7 ISR and 56.9 mIoU on the latter. The abstract also reports a 4.05-fold inference speedup. Together, the findings support encoding spatial relationships directly in the generation mechanism and refining the policy toward the criteria used to evaluate controllable image generation.
icml-2026-structmar-structure-aware-mask.tldr: StructMAR adds explicit spatial attention structure and policy refinement to improve object-layout alignment in masked autoregressive image generation.

paragraphs: A system that generates video and audio from text must coordinate several kinds of success: convincing pictures, plausible sound, timing between them, and adherence to the request. Evaluating each medium separately can miss failures in their relationship. T2AV-Compass provides a unified benchmark intended to test these requirements together.

The benchmark contains 500 diverse, complex prompts created through a taxonomy-driven process designed for semantic richness and physical plausibility. Its evaluation combines objective signal-level measurements of video quality, audio quality, and cross-modal alignment with judgments from a multimodal language model. The latter assess instruction following and realism, complementing the measurements of the generated signals.

An evaluation of 15 representative systems finds substantial gaps from human-level realism and cross-modal consistency, including among the strongest models tested. Persistent problems include unrealistic audio, imprecise synchronization, and failures to follow instructions. These results make the benchmark useful for diagnosing how systems fall short across interacting dimensions, rather than judging progress through the quality of video or audio alone.
icml-2026-t2av-compass-towards-unified-e.tldr: T2AV-Compass jointly evaluates generated audio and video, revealing persistent realism, synchronization, and instruction-following failures across 15 systems.

paragraphs: A molecule’s effect on a protein can depend on how it changes transitions between protein states, beyond how strongly it binds one structure. This distinction matters for generating agonists and antagonists, particularly for G protein-coupled receptors. The paper argues that optimizing static conformations does not capture the directional, non-reversible effects needed to distinguish these behaviors.

TD3B designs binder sequences using a directional transition-control objective. It combines a target-aware Direction Oracle with a soft gate for binding affinity and fine-tunes a pretrained discrete diffusion model. These components let the generation objective address the desired direction of functional change while also accounting for whether the proposed binder interacts with the target.

The framework enables targeted agonist and antagonist generation with functional directionality decoupled from binding affinity. The abstract reports that this capability is unattainable by the equilibrium-based or inference-only guidance baselines considered. The contribution is therefore a change in what binder generation optimizes: it explicitly targets how binding influences state transitions, giving the desired functional behavior a separate role in sequence design.
icml-2026-td3b-transition-directed-discr.tldr: TD3B generates binder sequences by targeting directional protein-state transitions, separating desired agonist or antagonist behavior from binding affinity.

paragraphs: Behavior cloning learns a policy from expert demonstrations. When autoregressive models are used for continuous control, continuous actions are commonly converted into discrete choices through quantization. This paper studies the theoretical consequences of that conversion: how approximation errors accumulate across a sequence of decisions and how they interact with the amount of training data needed.

The authors show that behavior cloning with quantized actions and log-loss achieves optimal sample complexity, matching existing lower bounds, while quantization error has only polynomial dependence on the horizon. This result requires stable dynamics and a probabilistic smoothness condition on the policy. The analysis also identifies when different quantization schemes satisfy or violate the requirements, connecting the guarantee to concrete choices in representing actions.

A model-based augmentation provably improves the error bound without requiring policy smoothness. The paper also establishes fundamental limits that account jointly for quantization error and statistical complexity. Together, these results explain conditions under which discretized action modeling is theoretically well supported and identify how representation error and learning from finite data constrain its performance.
icml-2026-understanding-behavior-cloning.tldr: The paper establishes optimal sample complexity and controlled quantization-error growth for behavior cloning under stability and policy-smoothness conditions.

paragraphs: A model can answer a question about a long video correctly while inventing the order of events in its explanation. Rewarding only final-answer correctness cannot distinguish that behavior from grounded reasoning. VideoTrace-R1 addresses the intermediate temporal claims themselves, seeking correspondence between the video’s event sequence and the model’s reasoning sequence.

Temporal Reasoning Traces provide a structured index of ordered event chains with deterministic operations for checking temporal claims. The authors combine this representation with temporal-enhanced GRPO, a reinforcement-learning procedure that assigns reward separately to typed blocks of reasoning. Each block is evaluated through a corresponding symbolic operation on the trace, allowing fabricated chronology to be detected at the claim level.

The model achieves state-of-the-art performance across long-video reasoning benchmarks, with its largest gains on out-of-domain tasks including Video-Holmes, CG-Bench-Reasoning, and VRBench. These findings support using programmatically checkable intermediate evidence as a learning signal. The approach makes chronological grounding part of what training rewards, so a correct final response does not by itself conceal unsupported temporal steps.
icml-2026-videotrace-r1-long-video-based.tldr: VideoTrace-R1 improves long-video reasoning by symbolically checking and rewarding intermediate temporal claims against structured event traces.

paragraphs: Image detectors can perform well on familiar generators and still fail when confronted with a new generator or changed generation settings. This paper argues that larger training datasets alone do not solve the problem when they cover too little of the variation a generator can produce. It focuses on finding realistic images that expose detector weaknesses.

PROBE uses the detector as a critic to guide changes within the generator’s internal representation space. These modifications steer generation toward challenging regions while producing realistic samples that are difficult to classify. The resulting examples reveal failure cases that standard sampling seldom encounters and are then used to refine the detector.

Experiments across multiple benchmarks indicate improved generalization to unseen generators. The findings support actively shaping the training distribution around weaknesses in the detector, rather than relying solely on the volume of routinely generated examples. The contribution is a feedback process linking detection and generation: the detector helps identify informative variations, and those variations supply the evidence needed to improve its subsequent decisions.
icml-2026-where-detectors-fail-probing-g.tldr: PROBE uses detector feedback to generate realistic, difficult training examples that improve detection of images from unseen generators.
